paper_title: A microwave paraphoton and axion detection experiment with 300 dB electromagnetic shielding at 3 GHz
notes: Microwave light-shining-through-wall experiment at CERN (March 2012) constraining paraphoton/hidden photon kinetic mixing chi. Only a single representative exclusion point is explicitly given in the text/figure: at m_gamma' = 1.1e-5 eV, chi = 7.6e-9. The full exclusion curve appears in Fig. 2 but only this point has numerical values stated. Not a DM haloscope, so no DM density. This is an LSW experiment reporting chi, hence DarkPhoton. | Vision: The CERN microwave LSW exclusion region is a narrow downward-pointing V (triangle) centered near m_gamma' = 1.1e-5 eV (3 GHz). The tip of the sensitivity reaches chi = 7.6e-9 at m = 1.1e-5 eV as labeled in the figure. Because the cavities are tuned to a single resonant frequency, the limit is essentially a vertical narrow band near 1.07e-5 eV; the reported boundary points trace the minimum (lower envelope) of the exclusion triangle. Points are approximate readings from the log-log plot. | Calibration: No calibration needed
